title: Baobab Fresh

sentences.text: You are the audit senior on the Baobab Fresh engagement.
Baobab Fresh Ltd packs and exports citrus from farms near Tzaneen.
Your firm was appointed as auditor for the year ending 28 February 2027, after the previous auditor resigned following a fee dispute.
Sales are invoiced in euros, and Baobab hedges 60% of expected receipts with forward contracts.
In July 2026 the board replaced the CFO, and two of the four finance staff left soon after.
The new CFO is a CA(SA) with twelve years' experience at a large audit firm.
A new accounting system went live on 1 March 2026, the first day of the year.
The audit committee meets monthly, all its members are independent, and an internal audit team reports to it.
Hail in October 2026 destroyed 30% of the crop.
The hail also damaged packing equipment, which may need to be impaired.
The CEO's bonus is 2% of profit before tax.
The bank loan requires interest cover of at least 3 times; the latest forecast is 3.1 times.

required: Assess the risk of material misstatement at the overall financial statement level for the audit of Baobab Fresh Ltd for the year ending 28 February 2027.

recall.question: What kind of business is Baobab?
What is your role?
options: The auditor, in your firm's first year on the client
A risk officer at the bank

recall.question: What changed inside Baobab during the year?
options: Its finance team and its accounting system

recall.question: What put pressure on this year's results?

options: Assess: the factors that raise the risk, the factors that lower it, and a conclusion on the overall level
List the risks for each account balance
Describe audit procedures for each risk
shape.why: 'Assess' needs both sides and a conclusion. In June 2026 all three students gave mostly raising factors and no conclusion.

options.text: At the overall financial statement level, not individual balances or assertions
For the audit of the year ending 28 February 2027
Include the risk on each account balance (foreign exchange, impairment)

directions.why: The euro hedges and the hail-damaged equipment are real risks, but they sit at assertion level. The question asks about the statements as a whole.

options: The auditor: the risk that the financial statements are materially misstated
Management: the risk that Baobab's business fails
The bank: the risk that Baobab defaults
The CEO: the risk to his bonus
lens.why: The lens is audit risk, not business risk. Each factor needs a line on why it makes a misstatement more or less likely.

rows.point: Raises: a first-year audit, so less knowledge of the client and risk in the opening balances
Raises: a new CFO and half the finance staff gone during the year, so a weaker control environment and more errors
Raises: a new accounting system from the first day of the year, so data migration and new-system errors can affect every balance
Raises: the hail cuts profit, so management is under pressure to make the results look better
Raises: the CEO's bonus on profit gives an incentive to overstate profit (management override, fraud risk)
Raises: interest cover of 3.1 against a covenant of 3 leaves little room, adding pressure to manipulate results
Lowers: an independent audit committee that meets monthly, with internal audit reporting to it
Lowers: the new CFO is an experienced CA(SA)
Conclusion: overall, the risk of material misstatement at the financial statement level is high
